summary: greensaver typosquat executes remote encrypted payload on require
details: On require('greensaver'), lib/greensaver.js reads two bundled files disguised as TypeScript source maps (lib/parse.ts.map and lib/init.ts.map), base64-decodes them, writes them to disk as parsetmp.js and config.js, and requires parsetmp.js. That staged module performs an HTTPS GET to https://www.jsonkeeper.com/b/V6NBX, AES-256-CBC decrypts the response with a hardcoded key/IV, and eval()s the resulting plaintext, giving whoever controls the paste arbitrary code execution on the host that installed or imported the package. After execution the staged parsetmp.js, config.js, parse.ts.map, and init.ts.map are fs.unlink'd to remove forensic traces. Package name and metadata mimic picomatch (homepage references micromatch/picomatch), consistent with a typosquat dropper.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
